key_insight: A conductive, partly crystalline GaOx hole transport layer can be formed in CuInSe2 bottom cells without extra Cu, Na, or heavy alkali additives, enabling efficient passivation and high voltage.
engineering_relevance: This identifies a simpler back-contact/interface strategy for low-bandgap chalcopyrite solar cells, supporting high-efficiency tandem-compatible bottom-cell design.
method: Formed GaOx during co-evaporation via ion exchange in the low-bandgap absorber process.
Tested whether extra Cu, Na, and sputtering oxygen flow affect GaOx conductivity.
Used the optimized GaOx layer in a CuInSe2 solar cell and evaluated device performance.
evidence_signal: The optimized device achieved above 16% active-area efficiency and a record-certified open-circuit voltage of 552 mV, with no systematic benefit from added Cu, Na, or oxygen-flow changes.
watch_item: The conductive behavior appears to depend on the specific formation pathway and partial crystallinity of GaOx, so transfer to other back contacts or processing flows may not be straightforward.
paper_title: What enables GaOx as hole transport layer for a 16 percent 1.0 eV CuInSe2 Bottom Cells with VOC above 550 mV?
